items.followUp: Write the chemical formula of aluminium oxide and magnesium chloride.

rubric.why: Calcium phosphate must have the correct formula.
rubric.how: Check that the formula is Ca₃(PO₄)₂.

rubric.why: Sodium chloride must have the correct formula.
rubric.how: Check that the formula is NaCl.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: An atom is neutral because it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that an atom has no net charge.

rubric.why: An ion is charged and is formed when an atom gains or loses electrons.
rubric.description: Ion is charged due to electron gain or loss
rubric.how: Look for both the charged nature of an ion and its formation by electron gain or loss.

modelAnswer: An atom is electrically neutral because it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
An ion is a charged particle formed when an atom gains or loses electrons.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of sodium and explain what it shows.

rubric.why: Electronic configuration describes the arrangement or distribution of electrons.
rubric.how: Look for the idea of arranging or distributing electrons.

rubric.why: The arrangement is described in terms of shells or energy levels.
rubric.description: Electrons in shells or energy levels
rubric.how: Look for shells or energy levels as the locations of the electrons.

modelAnswer: Electronic configuration is the arrangement or distribution of an atom’s electrons in its shells (energy levels).

items.followUp: State two limitations of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s model could not explain why the atom remains stable despite orbiting electrons being expected to radiate energy and fall into the nucleus.
rubric.how: Look for the unexplained stability of the atom or the expected collapse of electrons into the nucleus.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s model could not explain the line spectra of atoms.
rubric.how: Look for the inability to explain atomic line spectra.

modelAnswer: It could not explain the stability of the atom: revolving electrons should radiate energy and eventually fall into the nucleus.
It could not explain the line spectra of atoms.

rubric.why: Atomic radius is a distance measured from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Look for the idea of a distance from the nucleus.

rubric.why: The atomic radius extends to the atom’s outermost shell.
rubric.how: Look for the outermost or valence shell as the endpoint.

modelAnswer: The atomic radius is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell of an atom.
